The Nasarawa State chapter of the Social Democratic Party has rejected allegations by the state government linking former Governor Tanko Al-Makura and former Inspector-General of Police, Abubakar Adamu, to the disruption of activities surrounding Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s visit to Lafia on Wednesday for the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally. The state government had accused youths allegedly connected to the two politicians of disrupting Shettima’s visit to the Emir of Lafia’s palace and the APC rally, and directed security agencies to investigate the incident and identify those responsible. However, the SDP, through the Director of Digital Media and Strategic Communications of the IGP M.A. Adamu Campaign Organisation, Otaru Douglas, described the allegations as irresponsible, politically motivated and an attempt to tarnish the reputations of the former governor and ex-IGP. In a statement issued on Wednesday night, Douglas said Adamu was nowhere near the venue of the incident and had no youth group acting on his behalf to embarrass the Vice-President. He also denied that Al-Makura had any involvement in the disruption, describing both men as respected figures who would not sponsor violence or disrespect constituted authorities. The SDP campaign organisation said the disruption reflected public dissatisfaction with the APC-led government in the state, rather than any plot by opposition politicians. The statement said, “We wish to state in unequivocal terms that the attempt by the Nasarawa State Government to link His Excellency, IGP Mohammed Abubakar Adamu (retd.), the candidate of the Social Democratic Party, and His Excellency, Senator Umaru Tanko Al-Makura, to the ugly incident that marred the visit of the Vice-President, Sen. Kashim Shettima, to Lafia is not only irresponsible, but a clear act of political cowardice and mischief. “For the avoidance of doubt, IGP Adamu was nowhere near the venue of the said incident and has no youth group acting on his behalf to embarrass the Vice-President.” The organisation further accused Governor Abdullahi Sule and the APC leadership in the state of failing to reconcile aggrieved party members, alleging that the crisis within the ruling party had contributed to the political tension. The group also urged President Bola Tinubu to take note of the alleged disaffection within the Nasarawa APC, saying the state government should respect Al-Makura, whom it described as a founding figure of the party in the state. Earlier, the state government had announced that the governor ordered security agencies to investigate the disruption and ensure that those responsible, including alleged sponsors, were brought to account. The governor gave the directive at an expanded security meeting at the Government House, Lafia, on Thursday, following reports of obstruction of the Vice-President’s convoy during his visit to the Emir and disturbances at the rally venue. The Secretary to the State Government, Labaran Magaji, had alleged that some youths wearing T-shirts bearing Al-Makura’s photograph obstructed the Vice-President’s convoy after the royal homage. He also alleged that suspected opposition supporters wearing APC-branded shirts gained access to the rally venue, chanted opposition slogans and threw an object towards the podium where the Vice-President and other dignitaries were standing. Sule said the investigation should identify not only those who allegedly carried out the disruption but also those who planned and sponsored it. He also called for an inquiry into the use of tear gas at the rally venue, particularly around the podium. The governor described the incident as an embarrassment to the state and the office of the Vice-President, warning that political disagreements should not degenerate into violence. The SDP, however, urged security agencies to investigate the incident objectively and avoid what it described as a politically motivated attempt to witch-hunt opposition figures. Collins Agwam
